title: Pausanias, Description of Greece 7.24 (English, A. R. Shilleto, 1886)

source.license: Public domain (Shilleto died 1894; Project Gutenberg text)

summary: Pausanias (2nd century CE) on the Achaean city of Helike, destroyed by earthquake and sea in 373 BCE, and on the kinds of earthquake. Helike is the best-attested ancient city drowned in a day; Atlantis writers cite it often.

tree.title: Pausanias 7.24: Helike destroyed by earthquake and flood
tree.summary: Pausanias places Helike by the sea near Aegium. After the Achaeans killed suppliants at its temple of Poseidon, an earthquake flattened it and the sea flooded the grove. He lists warning signs and kinds of earthquake, and compares the loss of Sipylus.
